definition: a large, grand building built to hold the body or bodies of dead people.

collocations.example: Tourists lined up to enter the ancient mausoleum at dawn.
The emperor was buried in a marble mausoleum near the river.

definition: a pale purple color.

collocations.example: The walls were painted a soft shade of mauve.
She arrived dressed in mauve from head to toe.

definition: an infectious disease that causes a fever and small red spots on the skin.

collocations.example: Unvaccinated children can easily catch measles from classmates.
Health officials rushed to contain a measles outbreak downtown.

definition: a dangerous type of skin cancer that can spread quickly.

collocations.example: People who tan often may develop melanoma later in life.
A melanoma diagnosis prompted him to avoid the midday sun.

definition: showing emotions or reactions that are much stronger than the situation deserves.

collocations.example: I don't want to sound melodramatic, but this could ruin us.
Her melodramatic reaction to the small delay surprised everyone.

definition: relating to trade or the business of buying and selling goods.

collocations.example: The city's wealthy mercantile class funded many public buildings.
The treaty was designed to protect the nation's mercantile interests.

definition: an imaginary line drawn from the North Pole to the South Pole on a map.

collocations.example: The prime meridian passes through Greenwich, near London.
As the ship sailed east, it crossed one meridian after another.

definition: the spread of cancer from the original place to other parts of the body.

collocations.example: Early treatment can help prevent metastasis to other organs.
Doctors monitor patients closely for the risk of metastasis.

definition: the scientific study of the weather and the atmosphere.

collocations.example: She went to college to study meteorology and climate science.
He earned a degree in meteorology before joining the news station.

definition: a small place or group that has the same qualities as something much larger.

collocations.example: The small town felt like a microcosm of society as a whole.
The office drama showed national politics in microcosm.

definition: film used to store very small photographs of documents or pages.

collocations.example: The library chose to store old newspapers on microfilm.
He loaded a roll of microfilm into the reading machine.

definition: a unit of length equal to one millionth of a meter.

collocations.example: The dust particles measured only a few microns across.
The filter traps micron-sized particles before they reach the engine.

definition: a unit of time equal to one thousandth of a second.

collocations.example: The signal reached the server in just a few milliseconds.
The system shuts down within milliseconds of detecting a fault.

definition: a very small freshwater fish.

collocations.example: The boy caught a tiny minnow in his cupped hands.
We watched minnows darting through the clear stream water.

definition: extremely small.

collocations.example: The recipe needs only a minuscule amount of salt.
The newborn kittens were minuscule in size and nearly hairless.

definition: an image of something, such as water, that appears in the distance but is not really there.

collocations.example: Exhausted hikers often see a mirage of water in the desert.
The distant city shimmered like a mirage in the heat.

definition: happiness and laughter; a feeling of fun and amusement.

collocations.example: The holiday party was full of mirth and loud laughter.
The whole room shook with mirth at his silly joke.

definition: a large padded glove used to catch the ball in baseball.

collocations.example: He oiled his baseball mitt before the first game of spring.
The ball smacked loudly into the catcher's mitt.

definition: relating to a verb form that shows possibility, necessity, or permission.

collocations.example: Words like 'can' and 'must' are each a modal verb.
Students often misuse the modal form in formal writing.

definition: a particular method or way of doing something, especially a type of medical treatment.

collocations.example: Doctors chose a gentler treatment modality for the elderly patient.
The hospital adopted a new imaging modality for early diagnosis.

definition: a soft-bodied animal without a backbone, such as a snail, clam, or squid.

collocations.example: The biologist collected a rare marine mollusk from the tide pool.
The beach was covered with broken mollusk shells.

definition: a seasonal wind that brings heavy rain to southern Asia in summer.

collocations.example: Farmers plant their crops at the start of the monsoon season.
Heavy monsoon rains flooded the streets of the coastal city.

definition: a series of short scenes or pictures put together to form one piece.

collocations.example: She created a photo montage of their trip for his birthday.
The film shows a training montage before the big fight.

definition: the customs and moral rules accepted by a particular group or society.

collocations.example: The novel gently mocks the social mores of its time.
The play questions the mores of modern society.

definition: a building or room where dead bodies are kept before burial or examination.

collocations.example: The detective headed to the city morgue to identify the victim.
The unclaimed body lay in the morgue for several weeks.

definition: unhappy, silent, and unwilling to talk; gloomy.

collocations.example: He looked morose all afternoon after hearing the bad news.
She sank into a morose mood that lasted for days.

definition: a small piece of food.

collocations.example: The stray cat begged for even a tiny morsel of food.
He ate every bit, down to the last morsel on his plate.

definition: to make someone feel very embarrassed or ashamed.

collocations.example: Being praised in public can mortify a shy person.
His rude joke utterly mortified the whole family.

definition: a place where dead bodies are kept before a funeral.

collocations.example: The bodies were taken to the hospital mortuary overnight.
She trained for two years to work at a mortuary.

definition: made up of many different types of people or things that do not seem to belong together.

collocations.example: A motley crew of volunteers showed up to clean the park.
His shelf held a motley collection of books and souvenirs.

definition: a dead body that has been preserved, especially one wrapped in cloth in ancient Egypt.

collocations.example: The museum displayed an Egyptian mummy in a glass case.
Scientists carefully unwrapped the mummy to study its bones.

definition: a strong-smelling substance used to make perfume.

collocations.example: The night air was heavy with musk and jasmine.
The perfume had a warm hint of musk beneath the flowers.

definition: having a stale, damp, or moldy smell, often from being old or shut up.

collocations.example: The old basement had a musty smell of damp paper.
The abandoned cottage felt musty and damp inside.

definition: a condition in which a person sees near objects clearly but distant ones look blurry; nearsightedness.

collocations.example: Many children today suffer from myopia because of too much screen time.
Glasses or contact lenses can easily correct myopia.

definition: a person or thing that has the same name as another.

collocations.example: The boy was proud to be his grandfather's namesake.
The small restaurant is often confused with its famous namesake.

definition: just beginning to exist or develop.

collocations.example: The government offered support to the nation's nascent solar industry.
The technology is still in its nascent stage of development.

definition: the birth of Jesus Christ, or a scene or picture showing it.

collocations.example: The church set up a nativity scene in the courtyard at Christmas.
The children performed a nativity play for their parents.

definition: relating to ships, sailors, or sailing.

collocations.example: The lighthouse was about three nautical miles from the harbor.
The captain studied the nautical charts before setting sail.

definition: the small hollow in the middle of the stomach; the belly button.

collocations.example: She decided to pierce her navel on her eighteenth birthday.
He felt a sharp pain just below the navel.

definition: the death of cells or tissue in part of the body.

collocations.example: A lack of blood flow can lead to tissue necrosis.
The spider's venom can cause necrosis around the bite.

definition: able to be discussed and changed before an agreement is reached.

collocations.example: The seller said the price was negotiable if we paid in cash.
They offered a negotiable contract with flexible working hours.

definition: a mild mental illness involving strong anxiety or obsessive worry.

collocations.example: He developed a neurosis about germs after the long illness.
Many patients suffer from neurosis caused by constant stress.

definition: a chemical that carries signals between nerve cells in the brain and body.

collocations.example: Nerve cells release a neurotransmitter to pass along each signal.
Some drugs raise the levels of a neurotransmitter such as serotonin.

definition: a connection or central point that links several things together.

collocations.example: The city became a nexus of trade between three continents.
Researchers studied the nexus between poverty and poor health.

definition: a small, round lump or swelling, often found in the body.

collocations.example: The doctor found a small nodule on his thyroid during the exam.
Surgeons decided to remove the nodule for further testing.

definition: a loop of rope that tightens as it is pulled, often used for hanging.

collocations.example: The sailor knew how to tie a secure noose in the thick rope.
They placed a noose around the prisoner's neck.

definition: too interested in other people's private business.

collocations.example: Our nosy neighbor watches everyone who comes and goes.
Don't be so nosy about how much money I make.

definition: one of the basic building blocks that make up DNA and RNA.

collocations.example: Scientists compared the nucleotide sequence of the two viruses.
A change in a single nucleotide can cause a genetic disease.

definition: a beautiful young female spirit of nature in ancient Greek and Roman myths.

collocations.example: The legend tells of a water nymph living in the mountain spring.
Ancient poets wrote of a nymph of the forest guarding the grove.

definition: to treat a person as an object rather than as a human being with feelings.

collocations.example: The advertisement was criticized for the way it objectified women.
Social media can lead teenagers to constantly objectify themselves.

definition: a natural yellow or reddish-brown earth used as a pigment or color.

collocations.example: Ancient artists painted the cave walls with red ocher.
The desert cliffs glowed in a warm shade of ocher.

definition: a flat shape with eight straight sides and eight angles.

collocations.example: The park's fountain was built in the shape of an octagon.
A stop sign is a regular octagon with equal sides.

definition: a long poem that praises or expresses strong feelings about a person or thing.

collocations.example: The poet decided to write an ode to the autumn season.
The song is an ode to the singer's hometown.

definition: a medical condition in which the body swells because of extra fluid in the tissues.

collocations.example: A poor diet and long flights can cause edema in the legs.
The doctor prescribed medicine to reduce the edema.

definition: the tube in the body that carries food from the throat to the stomach.

collocations.example: Food travels down the esophagus to reach the stomach.
Smoking raises the risk of cancer of the esophagus.

definition: to perform the official duties at a ceremony or event.

collocations.example: A close friend agreed to officiate at their wedding.
She was the first woman to officiate a professional game.

definition: a smooth, oily substance rubbed on the skin to heal it or reduce pain.

collocations.example: The nurse applied ointment to the burn on his arm.
He bought a tube of ointment for his dry, cracked hands.

definition: the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

collocations.example: The equation ends with the Greek letter omega.
The unit of resistance is shown by a capital omega.

definition: the responsibility or duty to do something.

collocations.example: The onus is on the employer to provide a safe workplace.
The new rule puts the onus on drivers to check their tires.

definition: a type of strong drug used to relieve pain, which can be addictive.

collocations.example: Doctors have become careful about prescribing opioid painkillers.
He struggled for years with an opioid addiction.

definition: a sphere or ball, especially a large or glowing one.

collocations.example: A glowing orb of light hovered above the dark field.
The orb of the sun sank slowly behind the hills.

definition: the scientific study of birds.

collocations.example: He traveled the world to study ornithology in remote forests.
A professor of ornithology led the early-morning bird walk.

definition: to deliberately exclude someone from a group or society.

collocations.example: The team began to ostracize the player who broke the rules.
Villagers would socially ostracize anyone who ignored the old customs.

definition: a very large African bird that cannot fly but can run very fast.

collocations.example: An ostrich egg is larger than two dozen chicken eggs.
They visited an ostrich farm during their trip to South Africa.

definition: a large rock or group of rocks that stick out above the surface of the ground.

collocations.example: The climbers rested on a rock outcrop near the summit.
An outcrop of granite rose from the middle of the field.

definition: to do something better than someone or something else.

collocations.example: Each cook tried to outdo the others at the chili contest.
The band outdid themselves with a stunning final performance.

definition: very strange, unusual, or shocking.

collocations.example: At first the plan seemed like an outlandish idea.
The salesman made outlandish claims about the product.

definition: to live or last longer than someone or something else.

collocations.example: She outlived her husband by nearly twenty years.
The old software has long outlived its usefulness.

definition: no longer modern, useful, or acceptable; out of date.

collocations.example: The factory struggled with slow, outmoded equipment.
The policy is based on an outmoded idea of family life.

definition: to do better than someone or something else at a task or activity.

collocations.example: The new phone easily outperforms its competitors in speed.
The fund managed to outperform the market last year.

definition: a sudden, strong expression of emotion from many people.

collocations.example: His sudden death caused a huge outpouring of grief.
The news sparked a spontaneous outpouring from fans worldwide.

definition: to give someone or something too much to carry, do, or deal with.

collocations.example: Long shifts overburden workers and lead to costly mistakes.
Heavy traffic can overburden the system during peak hours.

definition: (of the sky or weather) covered with clouds; dull and gray.

collocations.example: They hiked all day under a gray, overcast sky.
The morning was cold, overcast, and gray.

definition: a state of very great activity or increased effort.

collocations.example: As the deadline neared, the whole team went into overdrive.
Her imagination shifted into overdrive as she wrote the story.

definition: to describe or explain something in a way that is too simple and misses important details.

collocations.example: Politicians often oversimplify the issue to win votes.
News reports tend to oversimplify complex scientific findings.

definition: larger than the usual or normal size.

collocations.example: She wore an oversized coat that reached her ankles.
The airline charges extra for oversized luggage.

definition: a chemical reaction in which a substance combines with oxygen, often causing rust or decay.

collocations.example: Rust forms through the slow process of oxidation.
A coat of paint helps prevent oxidation of the metal.

definition: to combine with oxygen, especially in a way that causes rust or decay.

collocations.example: Cut apples oxidize quickly and turn brown.
Salt water can oxidize metal parts on a boat.

definition: to make someone who is angry or upset become calm and peaceful.

collocations.example: The leader tried to pacify the angry crowd with a short speech.
She sang softly to pacify the crying child.

definition: a small field where horses are kept or exercised.

collocations.example: The foal ran happily around the grassy horse paddock.
Each morning they turn the horses out into the paddock.

definition: a field that is flooded with water and used for growing rice.

collocations.example: Farmers worked knee-deep in the flooded rice paddy.
They flood the paddy before planting the young rice.

definition: a lock with a U-shaped bar that can be attached to a door, gate, or chain.

collocations.example: He secured his locker with a combination padlock.
The owner put a padlock on the gate every night.

definition: relating to the medical care of babies and children.

collocations.example: The sick child was moved to the hospital's pediatric ward.
A gentle pediatric nurse calmed the frightened toddler.

definition: a round container with a handle for carrying liquids; a bucket.

collocations.example: The boy carried a heavy pail of water from the well.
She filled a pail with fresh milk from the cow.

definition: a medical condition that causes loss of movement or control in part of the body.

collocations.example: The child was born with cerebral palsy and uses a wheelchair.
After the stroke, he suffered from palsy on one side.

definition: very small or too little in amount to be useful or important.

collocations.example: They offered a paltry sum for all his hard work.
The workers protested against their paltry wages.

definition: something believed to solve all problems or cure all diseases; a cure-all.

collocations.example: Technology is not a panacea for every social problem.
The new law was wrongly seen as a panacea.

definition: an organ in the body that helps digestion and controls blood sugar.

collocations.example: The pancreas produces insulin to control blood sugar.
Cancer of the pancreas is difficult to detect early.

definition: to do or say what someone wants in order to please them, even if it is wrong.

collocations.example: The newspaper panders to its readers' worst fears.
The candidate shamelessly pandered to voters before the election.

definition: to move a camera steadily in one direction to follow something or show a wide view.

collocations.example: The director asked them to pan the camera across the crowd.
The shot slowly pans across the empty battlefield.

definition: the use of movements and gestures to express something without words.

collocations.example: He went through a pantomime of searching his pockets for the key.
The children acted out the whole story in pantomime.

definition: the position, authority, or period of office of the pope.

collocations.example: Many reforms were introduced during his papacy.
In the Middle Ages, the power of the papacy was immense.
